findings.how_to_check: In temp.dta, run `tab validated_before validated_after if status==1 & congruent==0, missing`. Observe that 15.8% of identical pairs change validation status solely due to differing 1940 middle initials between link files.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not describe the 65% to 84% rise as an increase in link match quality or proof of recovering true matches over spurious matches. Either validate links against an independent middle-initial source held fixed across both specifications, or describe the metric as middle-initial agreement that conflates transcription differences with link quality.
findings.title: Middle-initial validation rate increases by 15.8 percentage points for identical kept pairs, confounding the paper's claim of improved match quality
findings.what_the_code_does: The diagnostic shows that for kept links in the discordant sample (829,471 pairs linking the identical 1940 record to the identical 1930 record before and after), middle-initial validation rises from 63.4% (valKeptOldTarget) to 79.2% (valKeptTarget). This occurs because CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do:70-86 merges mi1940 from the Ancestry link file for validated_before and from the model link file for validated_after, altering the validator between the two evaluations.
findings.why_it_matters: The paper claims at lines 98 and 547-549 that the validation rate increase from 65% to 84% represents a 28% increase in match quality demonstrating that the model recovers true links rather than spurious ones. Because link correctness cannot change for identical kept pairs, the 15.8 percentage point increase is driven by changes in 1940 middle-initial transcription rather than link quality.

findings.how_to_check: Inspect replication/diagnostics/validation_by_link_status.log:344-346, which displays: `Target Added: links 1,953,052 with MI 396,760 validated 0.8611`. Compare this with validation_by_link_status.tex lines 31-32, where only nAddedTarget = 1,953,052 is output.
findings.suggested_fix: Output both the total link count and the count of links with observable middle initials (e.g., nAddedTargetWithMI = 396,760), along with the availability percentage (20.3%). When discussing validation of added links in the paper, explicitly disclose that the 86.1% rate applies only to the selected 20.3% subset with observable initials.
findings.title: 86.1% added-link validation rate applies only to a selected 20.3% subsample with observed initials, but committed macro reports full link count
findings.what_the_code_does: For added links in the target sample (`status==3 & congruent==0`), `summarize validated_after` calculates an 86.1% validation rate over 396,760 records with observable middle initials. However, line 68 outputs `repnum nAddedTarget = 1,953,052` from `count if status==3`, discarding the non-missing count r(N).
findings.why_it_matters: Middle initial presence is not random and correlates with literacy, race, and socioeconomic status. The 86.1% agreement rate describes only 20.3% of added links; the remaining 79.7% (1.56 million links) cannot be validated by middle initials. Pairing `\valAddedTarget = 86.1` with `\nAddedTarget = 1,953,052` masks this missingness and invites claims that nearly 2 million added links are validated at 86%.

review_limits: External census microdata and raw link files were not re-executed from scratch; runtime figures were validated from the committed Stata diagnostic log and intermediate datasets on disk.
The paper draft resides in a separate repository (D:/repos/6638fa0fd89fbec05130caeb) outside this git commit range; claims were verified against its current on-disk LaTeX text.
Machine B linkage code (LINKAGE/code/) was not modified in HEAD~1..HEAD and was examined only to trace the derivation of mi1930 and mi1940.
Raw census images and human transcription adjudication are unavailable, so character-level accuracy of transcribed name strings cannot be audited.
summary: The commit implements a useful decomposition of middle-initial validation across kept, switched, added, and dropped links, but it reveals that the validation rate increases substantially (63.4% to 79.2%) even for identical kept pairs due to changing 1940 middle-initial transcriptions. Additionally, the reported 86.1% validation rate for added links applies to only 20.3% of links with observable initials, and a duplicate macro definition in the generated TeX file breaks the repository's automated claim-checking script. The most important fix is to avoid interpreting middle-initial validation gains as evidence of link accuracy when the validating field itself varies across transcriptions.
